verses.text: Then King David said to the whole assembly, "My son Solomon, the one God has chosen, is still young and has no experience. The work is great, because this palace is not for a human being. It is for the LORD God.

With all my strength I have provided for the house of my God: gold for the gold things, silver for the silver things, bronze for the bronze things, iron for the iron things, and wood for the wooden things. I have also provided onyx stones, stones for setting, shiny stones of many colours, all kinds of precious stones, and large amounts of marble.

Besides all this, because I love the house of my God, I am giving my own treasure of gold and silver to the house of my God. This is in addition to everything I have already provided for this holy house.
I am giving about one hundred tonnes of gold from Ophir and about two hundred and forty tonnes of refined silver to cover the walls of the buildings,
and for all the gold and silver work to be done by the craftsmen. Now, who else is willing to give himself to the LORD today?"
Then the leaders of the families, the leaders of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work gave willingly.

For the work on God's temple they gave about one hundred and seventy tonnes of gold and ten thousand gold coins, about three hundred and forty tonnes of silver, about six hundred and ten tonnes of bronze, and about three thousand four hundred tonnes of iron.
Anyone who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the LORD's temple, which was in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
The people were full of joy because their leaders had given so willingly. They had given to the LORD with all their hearts. King David was also very happy.
Then David praised the LORD in front of the whole assembly. He said, "Praise be to you, LORD, the God of our father Israel, forever and ever!
Yours, LORD, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty. Everything in heaven and on earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, LORD. You are honoured as the ruler over all.
Wealth and honour come from you, and you rule over everything. Power and strength are in your hands. You can make anyone great and give strength to all.
So now, our God, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give so willingly like this? Everything comes from you, and we have only given you what came from your own hand.
We are like strangers and visitors in your sight, as all our ancestors were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and they do not last.
LORD our God, all this wealth we have provided to build a house to honour your holy name comes from your hand. It all belongs to you.

I know, my God, that you test the heart and are pleased when people are honest. I have given all these things willingly and with an honest heart. And now I have seen with joy how your people here have given so willingly to you.
LORD, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep this desire in the hearts of your people forever, and keep their hearts loyal to you.
Give my son Solomon a heart that is completely true, so he will keep your commands, your teachings, and your laws, and do everything needed to build the palace I have provided for."
Then David said to the whole assembly, "Now praise the LORD your God!" So the whole assembly praised the LORD, the God of their ancestors. They bowed down low before the LORD and before the king.

The next day they offered sacrifices and burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, along with their drink offerings, and many other sacrifices for all Israel.

That day they ate and drank with great joy in the LORD's presence. Then they made David's son Solomon king a second time. They anointed him before the LORD to be ruler, and they anointed Zadok to be priest.
So Solomon sat on the LORD's throne as king in place of his father David. He was successful, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the leaders, the mighty warriors, and all of King David's sons promised to be loyal to King Solomon.
The LORD made Solomon very great in the eyes of all Israel. He gave him royal majesty greater than any king of Israel before him.
David son of Jesse ruled over all Israel.
He ruled over Israel for forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, after a long life full of wealth and honour. His son Solomon became king after him.
Everything King David did, from beginning to end, is written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet, and the records of Gad the seer.
These records tell about his whole rule, his power, and the things that happened to him, to Israel, and to all the kingdoms of the other lands.
